messages:
Maria Chen: Quick follow-up on adapter granularity for Hosted/Dedicated/Private. We need to decide how coarse adapters are -- per-deployment-type vs per-capability. Thoughts?

Kevin Patel: I'd prefer capability-based (model-serving, auth, telemetry) so shared logic can be reused across deployments.

Leah Gomez: +1, but ops perspective: Hosted uses our auth tokens, Private relies on customer KMS & LDAP, so adapter needs explicit hooks for auth translation.

Arjun Rao: Agreed. Suggest pattern: thin environment shim that maps control-plane configs -> runtime config. Adapter = shim + capability impls.

Kevin Patel: Concern: performance overhead of shims at request path. Need to avoid adding allocations on hot path. Can we compile shims away at build-time for Dedicated/Private packages?

Maria Chen: Yes. Two levels: 1) compile-time specialization (for private builds), 2) runtime feature flags for hosted where we need dynamic routing.

Leah Gomez: Ops question: telemetry - do we normalize metrics names across modalities? Hosted uses tenant_id, Dedicated has pool_id, Private has org_id. We should normalize with labels.

Arjun Rao: proposal: canonical metric names with tags: {scope_type: 'tenant'|'pool'|'org', scope_id: <id>}

Kevin Patel: That works, but we must ensure no PII leakage from org_id. Sanitize and hash externally.

Maria Chen: Also need to define contract for fallback model variants across deployments. Hosted auto-fallback to cheaper variant; Dedicated should optionally allow that but owner-controlled; Private must be opt-in.

Leah Gomez: UX: policy per route: {fallback_allowed: bool, fallback_order: [variants], cost_threshold: int}

Arjun Rao: Implementation note: control-plane exposes a declarative policy proto. Runtime adapters implement evaluate_policy(request, context) -> variant.

Maria Chen: sample proto snippet:
```
message FallbackPolicy {
  bool fallback_allowed = 1;
  repeated string fallback_order = 2;
  int32 cost_threshold = 3;
}
```

Kevin Patel: We need versioning for the proto. Also migration plan for older agents.

Leah Gomez: Ops: rolling upgrade path for Dedicated clusters. Can adapter reject unknown policy fields gracefully.

Arjun Rao: yes, adapters must ignore unknown fields and log warnings. Also provide a feature-negotiation endpoint: /adapter/capabilities -> JSON list

infra-bot: Canary deploy started for adapter-v2 to staging

Maria Chen: Good. One more: secret management. Private uses customer KMS so adapter must include secret-lookup abstraction: get_secret(key, scope) -> value or error. No secret should flow to hosted control-plane logs.

Kevin Patel: Affirm. Add audit hook with sampling. Also define SLA semantics: latency budgets for adapter operations (auth check, secret fetch) must be in ms and documented.

Leah Gomez: Last ops ask: trace correlation between control plane and private runtime. Need consistent trace_id propagation across shims.

Arjun Rao: add header X-Redwood-Trace and ensure adapters forward it. If missing, generate deterministic trace based on request id.

Maria Chen: Ok action items:
- Arjun: draft adapter proto + capability endpoint (ETA Tue)
- Kevin: benchmark shim overhead and sketch build-time specialization (ETA Wed)
- Leah: telemetry tag spec + ops playbook (ETA Thu)
- Maria: write RFC summarizing policy and secret UX (ETA Fri)

Kevin Patel: I'll join for the RFC review.

Leah Gomez: I'll do runbook review as well.

Maria Chen: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Arjun Rao: I'll open PRs once proto is drafted.

remind-bot: Reminder set for Tue 09:00 to check PR
